arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: the side that brought the case asserts Article 10(a) allows postal service if the forum state authorizes it.
the side that brought the case claims the receiving state must not have objected to the provision.
the opposing side contends the treaty text is unambiguous and restricts this service method.
Justice Alito noted treaties are also United States law requiring standard interpretation rules.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the scope of the Hague Service Convention. It asks if domestic law controls mail service when the treaty is silent on objections.
